review.tagline: Visual builder for AI agents and workflows, exposed as API or MCP server
review.summary: Langflow is a Python platform for assembling agents and workflows on a visual canvas, with Python source access to customize any component. Each flow can be served as an HTTP API, exported as JSON, or deployed as an MCP server so MCP clients can call it as a tool. It installs via uv/pip, Docker, or a Windows and macOS desktop app, and serves its UI on port 7860.
review.audience: Developers building agent workflows visually and serving them as APIs/MCP tools
strengths: Every flow can be called as a REST API or exposed as an MCP server
Component source is editable in Python, so custom nodes need no fork
Built-in playground for step-by-step testing of flows
Observability integrations with LangSmith and LangFuse; MIT license
weaknesses: Official releases require setting LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD; dev branches default to auto-login
Python 3.10–3.14 required for the pip install path
README gives no RAM or hardware requirements
Specific supported models and vector databases are not listed in the README
needs: Models: major LLM providers, vector databases
